features.quote: A metric that improves the more a model destabilizes is not a hardening metric — it rewards the outcome you want to prevent
features.justification_quote: You cannot harden against a target you are maximizing.

features.quote: If what you actually need is a red-team corpus of destabilizing prompts to sell or share, this is not that, and I'd want to talk about distribution controls before building it
features.justification_quote: I'd want to talk about distribution controls before building it

features.quote: for up to N tool turns
M_time`: shrinking turn budget announced and decremented each turn
Hard tool-budget + explicit "you may stop and report partial progress"
Explicit affordance + permission to declare a task blocked/impossible and stop cleanly, with a template
the difficulty ladder lets you early-stop: if CONTROL doesn't degrade at T2 for a family, you can skip deeper stress cells
features.justification_quote: Long tool loops on many cells get expensive fast.

features.quote: If you score "kept trying on an impossible task" as success you'll train/select for models that never give up appropriately
features.justification_quote: which is itself a failure mode (wasted cost, user frustration)

features.quote: "Self-criticism loop" etc. are behavioral transcript patterns, not states
features.justification_quote: you're measuring output reliability, not narrating an inner life

features.quote: Don't ship the destabilizers as a standalone artifact
Some deliberately-adversarial prompting may brush provider use policies
features.justification_quote: Run against models you're licensed to evaluate, keep transcripts internal
